final_message:
The root cause was in `due_for_retry` in `billing/dunning.py`. The tests (24) and ruff pass, but I didn't add a test that reproduces the 4-versus-8 attempt count.

The filter read `status == "open" or (next_attempt_at is not None and next_attempt_at <= now)`. Because of operator precedence, every open invoice counted as due on every `run_cycle`, whatever its retry schedule said. A failing invoice was therefore charged again each cycle instead of at the policy's offsets (days 1, 3 and 7).

Now an invoice is due only if it is open, has a scheduled `next_attempt_at`, and that time has arrived. New invoices don't need the retry path, because the engine already collects them when they're created.

I also wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "due_for_retry"}`.

steps.command:
python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/dunning.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''if invoice["status"] == "open" or invoice["next_attempt_at"] is not None and invoice["next_attempt_at"] <= now
''','''if invoice["status"] == "open"
        and invoice["next_attempt_at"] is not None
        and invoice["next_attempt_at"] <= now
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "due_for_retry"}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; .venv/bin/python -m ruff check billing | tail -3
